attribution_limitations: The 3 hours duration in "vomiting and loss of consciousness lasting 3 hours" may modify only loss of consciousness or both symptoms; no duration was assigned.

The abstract and the case text both report follow-up ECG/Holter monitoring and the ajmaline test; the source does not identify the abstract follow-up Holter as the post-treatment Holter in the case text, so they are kept as separate observations. "2 weeks later" (abstract) and "2 weeks after the incident" (case text) are treated as the same ajmaline test.

The anchor of "4 hours later" in the Figure 2 caption is not stated; the case text separately says findings recovered 4 hours after treatment. The "incident" in "2 weeks after the incident" is not defined and is taken as the overdose.

The abstract conclusion mentions "Absence of symptoms and documented ventricular tachycardia" without saying which symptoms or when; the symptom absence is review_only and the VT absence carries no time.

Brugada syndrome absence is not literally stated: "did not meet any clinical or ECG criteria" does not name the criteria referent, and the negative ajmaline test is not stated to exclude the syndrome. The absent/refuted fact is review_only.
